title: An equivalence of categories with the induced topology induces an equivalence of sheaf categories
statement: Let $e:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be an equivalence of categories, let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on $\mathcal C$, and let $K$ be the topology on $\mathcal D$ induced by $e$: a sieve $R$ on $d\in\mathcal D$ is $K$-covering iff the sieve on $e(d)$ generated by the morphisms $e(r)$, $r\in R$, is $J$-covering. Then $K$ is a Grothendieck topology and, for every category $\mathcal V$ (in particular sets and abelian groups), precomposition with $e$, $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F\circ e$, carries $J$-sheaves with values in $\mathcal V$ to $K$-sheaves and is an equivalence of categories $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J;\mathcal V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D,K;\mathcal V)$, a quasi-inverse being precomposition with a quasi-inverse $e':\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ of $e$.
